mainTopic: קדשים קלים in sight of שילה, the שכינה in בנימין's land, and the years of the משכן in each place
overview: In the time of the משכן in שילה, קדשים קלים could be eaten anywhere שילה could be seen. The גמרא gives three hints for this rule: the place name תאנת שילה, רבי אבהו's reading of 'עלי עין' in יעקב's blessing, and רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא's reading of 'סנה' in משה's blessing. Next it defines 'seeing.' A ברייתא requires a full view with nothing blocking, while רב פפא says seeing part of it is enough. Two questions about borderline views end in תיקו. Then רב דימי reports in רבי's name that the שכינה always rested in בנימין's land, even at שילה. רב יוסף objects from פסוקים that call שילה 'the tent of יוסף.' The answer is that a strip of יוסף's land reached into בנימין's land, and the question turns out to be a מחלוקת תנאים. Finally a ברייתא counts the years the משכן stood in each place: 39 in the מדבר, 14 in גלגל, 57 in נוב and גבעון, and 369 in שילה. The גמרא proves each number in turn, and the count of the 57 years continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The name תאנת שילה hints at eating sacrifices in sight of שילה
steps.stepSummary: The place name תאנת שילה is read as 'the place where people sigh over שילה,' because they used to eat קדשים there.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק mentions 'Taanath Shiloh.' It is called that because it is a place where anyone who sees שילה sighs about the sacrifices that used to be eaten there.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a hint from a place name in ספר יהושע to show that קדשים קלים were eaten in places that could see שילה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word תאנת sounds like מתאנח, 'sighing.' People standing there sighed after שילה was destroyed. That means they used to eat sacrifices from that spot, which was within sight of שילה.

keyTerms.meaning: A place near שילה named in ספר יהושע

phrases.english: "[And the border went] to Taanath Shiloh"
phrases.notes: יהושע 16:6

phrases.english: a place where anyone who sees it [שילה]
sighs over it
phrases.notes: The name תאנת sounds like מתאנח, 'sighing.' That sound-alike is the whole hint.

phrases.english: about the eating of sacrifices it used to have.

steps.mimraCoreRuling: Places within sight of שילה were places where קדשים קלים were eaten, as the name תאנת שילה hints.

steps.title: רבי אבהו's hint from יעקב's blessing to יוסף
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבהו reads 'בן פרת עלי עין' as a reward to יוסף: sacrifices may be eaten in his portion as far as the eye can see.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אבהו said the hint is in the פסוק 'יוסף is a fruitful son by a fountain (עין).' The eye that refused to enjoy what was not its own will be rewarded: food will be eaten as far as that eye can see.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אבהו gives a different source for the rule. He reads the word עין in יעקב's blessing to יוסף as 'eye.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: עין means both 'fountain' and 'eye.' יוסף's eye did not reach for something that wasn't his. So as a reward, in his land (where שילה stood), קדשים may be eaten anywhere the eye can see the משכן.

keyTerms.meaning: A fruitful son, part of יעקב's blessing to יוסף
Both 'fountain' and 'eye'; the drasha plays on this
As far as its eyes can see

phrases.english: Rabbi Abahu said: the verse says:
"Joseph is a fruitful son,
a fruitful son by a fountain"
phrases.notes: בראשית 49:22. The word עין means 'fountain' here, but it also means 'eye.'

phrases.english: An eye that did not want
to feed on and enjoy
something that was not his,
phrases.notes: This is talking about יוסף turning down אשת פוטיפר.

phrases.english: will merit to eat
as far as its eyes can see.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a second source for the same rule
steps.mimraCoreRuling: As a reward for יוסף's restrained eye, קדשים may be eaten in his portion anywhere שילה can be seen.

steps.title: רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא's hint from משה's blessing
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא reads 'שכני סנה' as 'among the haters' (שנואין). The eating reaches even into other tribes' land, as long as שילה can be seen.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא said the hint is in 'the favor of Him Who dwells in the bush (סנה).' The eye that refused to enjoy what was not its own will be rewarded: food will be eaten even among the haters.
steps.whatsHappening: A third source is given, this time from משה's blessing to יוסף. It adds that the eating can happen even outside יוסף's own land.
steps.deeperAnalysis: סנה sounds like שנואין, 'haters.' The 'haters' are the tribes of the brothers who hated יוסף. So קדשים could be eaten even in their land, if שילה was visible from there. This goes further than רבי אבהו's version.

keyTerms.meaning: The burning bush; sounds like שנואין
The One Who dwelt in the bush (ה׳)

phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei son of Rabbi Chanina said:
"And the favor of Him Who dwelt in the bush"
phrases.notes: דברים 33:16. סנה, 'bush,' sounds like שנואין, 'haters.'

phrases.english: An eye that did not want to enjoy
something that was not his,
will merit to eat even among the haters.
phrases.notes: The 'haters' are the other tribes, whose fathers hated יוסף.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A parallel drasha using the same 'restrained eye' idea, from a different פסוק
steps.mimraCoreRuling: קדשים may be eaten anywhere שילה is visible, even in other tribes' land.
steps.whatToRemember: Three hints teach the same rule: the name תאנת שילה, the word עין in יעקב's blessing, and the word סנה in משה's blessing. The last two both reward יוסף's eye for not taking what wasn't his.

steps.title: A ברייתא defines 'seeing' as seeing all of it, with nothing blocking
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא explains that 'seeing' שילה means having a full view, with no barrier in between.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught: the 'seeing' that was mentioned means seeing all of it, with nothing blocking between the person and the place.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now moves from finding the source to defining the term 'רואה' (seeing) used in the rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This sets a strict standard. A partial or blocked view does not count. Only a clear, complete view of שילה makes a place one where קדשים may be eaten.

keyTerms.meaning: Seeing; a place that has a view of

phrases.english: It was taught: the "seeing" that they mentioned
means seeing all of it,
and nothing blocks between him and it.

steps.mimraCoreRuling: רואה means a full, unblocked view.

steps.title: An example: the synagogue of מעון
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון בן אליקים illustrates the ברייתא's 'full view' with the synagogue of מעון.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמעון בן אליקים said to רבי אלעזר: I'll explain it to you. It's like the synagogue of מעון.
steps.whatsHappening: A real-life example is given to show what a 'full view with nothing blocking' looks like.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Nothing new is added to the law here. The example helps picture the ברייתא's strict standard: a spot with a completely open view of the place nearby.

keyTerms.meaning: I will explain it to you

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן אֶלְיָקִים לְרַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר,
phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon ben Elyakim said to Rabbi Elazar:
I will explain it to you:
for example, the synagogue of Maon.
phrases.notes: From there you had a clear, open view of the nearby town. That is the kind of 'seeing' he means.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן אֶלְיָקִים לְרַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר, אַסְבְּרָא לָךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Illustrates the ברייתא's definition
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The synagogue of מעון is a model of a full, unblocked view.

steps.title: רב פפא: seeing part of it is enough
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא says 'seeing' does not need a full view. Seeing even part of שילה is enough.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said: the 'seeing' that was mentioned does not mean seeing all of it. Seeing part of it is enough.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא gives a more lenient definition of 'seeing' than the ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא needed a complete view. רב פפא is satisfied with a partial view. That widens the area where קדשים קלים could be eaten.
steps.confusionAlert: רב פפא's view is the opposite of the ברייתא's. The ברייתא says you must see all of it; רב פפא says seeing some of it is enough.

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said: the "seeing" that they mentioned
does not mean seeing all of it,
but even seeing part of it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with the ברייתא's strict definition
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A partial view of שילה is enough for רואה.
steps.whatToRemember: There are two views of 'seeing' שילה. The ברייתא says a full, unblocked view (like the synagogue of מעון). רב פפא says a partial view is enough.

steps.title: Seeing שילה while standing but not while sitting
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא asks: if a person sees שילה only when standing, but not when sitting, does that count as 'seeing'?
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא asked: if from a certain spot a person standing can see שילה, but sitting down he cannot, what is the law?
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא asks a follow-up question about the rule of 'seeing' שילה from the earlier steps.
steps.deeperAnalysis: We already know that seeing even part of שילה is enough. Now the question is about a person's position. If the view depends on standing up, does that spot still count as a place from which שילה 'can be seen'?

keyTerms.meaning: He asked (a real question, not an attack)

phrases.english: Rav Pappa asked:
If he stands, he sees [שילה];
if he sits, he does not see – what is the law?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on רב פפא's own rule (step 6) that partial seeing is enough, and asks about a borderline case.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does a view of שילה that exists only while standing count as 'seeing'?

steps.title: Seeing שילה from the bank but not from inside the stream
steps.stepSummary: רבי ירמיה asks a similar question: a person on the bank of a stream sees שילה, but down inside the stream he cannot.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי ירמיה asked: if a person standing on the bank of a stream can see שילה, but down inside the stream he cannot, what is the law?
steps.whatsHappening: A second borderline question about 'seeing', this time about the shape of the ground rather than how a person holds himself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the block comes from the land itself: the low streambed hides שילה. The question is whether the inside of the stream counts as a 'seeing' place because the bank right next to it does.

keyTerms.meaning: On the bank of the stream
Inside the stream (down in the streambed)

phrases.english: Rabbi Yirmeya asked:
If he stands on the bank of the stream, he sees [שילה];
inside the stream he does not see – what is the law?
phrases.notes: The word in round brackets, 'sitting', is in some printed versions, but the corrected wording leaves it out.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A parallel question to רב פפא's, moving from body position to the shape of the land.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does a low spot that cannot see שילה count, if the higher spot right next to it can?

steps.title: Both questions stay unanswered
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא ends both questions with תיקו: they remain unresolved.
steps.simpleTranslation: Let it stand: no answer is found.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא closes both questions without deciding them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: No source settles whether these borderline spots count as 'seeing' שילה. Both questions about רב פפא's and רבי ירמיה's cases stay open.

keyTerms.meaning: Let it stand: the question is left without an answer

steps.whatToRemember: Seeing even part of שילה is enough (רב פפא). But whether a view that depends on standing up, or on being on the bank and not in the stream, counts is left as תיקו.

phrases.english: Let it stand [unresolved].

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Ends both questions without a decision.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The borderline cases of 'seeing' שילה stay undecided.

steps.title: The שכינה always rested in בנימין's land
steps.stepSummary: רב דימי reports in the name of רבי: in every place the שכינה rested (שילה, נוב and גבעון, the בית המקדש), it was in the land of בנימין, based on 'חופף עליו כל היום'.
steps.simpleTranslation: When רב דימי came, he said in the name of רבי: The שכינה rested on ישראל in three places: שילה, נוב and גבעון, and the Eternal House. In all of them it rested only in the land of בנימין, as the פסוק says, 'He covers him all the day', meaning all the 'coverings' will be only in בנימין's portion.
steps.whatsHappening: A new topic opens: רב דימי brings a teaching about which tribe's land held the שכינה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי reads 'חופף עליו', said in משה's blessing to בנימין, as 'covering' him with the שכינה. 'כל היום', all the day, is read as all the time periods. So every resting place of the שכינה in history was in בנימין's land.

keyTerms.meaning: Nov and Givon, sites of the משכן after שילה, counted here as one place
The Eternal House: the בית המקדש in ירושלים

steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up the next challenge: שילה is usually linked with יוסף's land, so saying it was in בנימין's land needs defending.

phrases.english: When Rav Dimi came,
he said that Rabbi said:

phrases.aramaic: בִּשְׁלֹשָׁה מְקוֹמוֹת שָׁרְתָה שְׁכִינָה עַל יִשְׂרָאֵל –
phrases.english: In three places the Divine Presence rested on Israel –
in Shiloh, and Nov and Givon, and the Eternal House;

phrases.aramaic: וּבְכוּלָּן לֹא שָׁרְתָה אֶלָּא בְּחֵלֶק בִּנְיָמִין.
phrases.english: and in all of them it rested only in the portion of Binyamin.
As it says: "He covers him all the day" –
phrases.notes: דברים 33:12

phrases.aramaic: כׇּל חֲפִיפוֹת לֹא יְהוּ אֶלָּא בְּחֶלְקוֹ שֶׁל בִּנְיָמִין.
phrases.english: all coverings will be only in the portion of Binyamin.

steps.triggerLanguage: כִּי אֲתָא רַב דִּימִי, אָמַר רַבִּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new topic after the תיקו closed the 'seeing' discussion.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Every resting place of the שכינה was in the land of בנימין.

steps.title: רב יוסף objects: שילה belonged to יוסף
steps.stepSummary: אביי repeats רב דימי's teaching to רב יוסף, who sharply rejects it, citing פסוקים that link the משכן in שילה with the tent of יוסף and the tribe of אפרים.
steps.simpleTranslation: When אביי went, he said this teaching before רב יוסף. רב יוסף said: כייליל had one son, and he is not right. But it is written, 'He forsook the משכן of שילה', and it is written, 'He rejected the tent of יוסף and did not choose the tribe of אפרים'!
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף challenges רבי's statement that שילה was in בנימין's land.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The two פסוקים come from the same psalm. When it describes ה׳ leaving שילה, it calls it 'the tent of יוסף' and 'the tribe of אפרים'. That suggests the משכן in שילה stood in יוסף's land, not בנימין's.

keyTerms.meaning: Before him, in front of him
But isn't it written? (opens a challenge from a פסוק)

phrases.english: When Abaye went,
he said it before Rav Yosef.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר: חַד בְּרָא הֲוָה לֵיהּ לְכַיְילִיל,
phrases.english: He said: Kaylil had one son,
phrases.notes: כייליל was אביי's father, so רב יוסף is talking about אביי himself.

phrases.english: and he is not right.
But isn't it written: "He forsook the Tabernacle of Shiloh",
phrases.notes: תהלים 78:60

phrases.english: and it is written: "He rejected the tent of Yosef
phrases.notes: תהלים 78:67

phrases.english: and did not choose the tribe of Ephraim"!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks רבי's claim from step 10 as it applies to שילה.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that the שכינה in שילה rested in בנימין's land.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The psalm calls the abandoned שילה 'the tent of יוסף' and links it to אפרים, so the משכן was in יוסף's land.

steps.title: רב אדא: the משכן spread across both tribes
steps.stepSummary: רב אדא answers that there is no difficulty. The שכינה could have been in בנימין's land and the סנהדרין in יוסף's land, just as in the בית המקדש the שכינה was in בנימין's land and the סנהדרין in יהודה's.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אדא said: What is his difficulty? Perhaps the שכינה was in בנימין's portion and the Great סנהדרין in יוסף's portion, since we find in the בית המקדש that the שכינה was in בנימין's portion and the סנהדרין in יהודה's portion!
steps.whatsHappening: רב אדא defends רבי's teaching against רב יוסף's challenge.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The site at שילה could have crossed a tribal border. The part where the שכינה rested was in בנימין's land, while the סנהדרין next to it was in יוסף's land, which is why the פסוק can call it 'the tent of יוסף'. The בית המקדש proves such a split happens: the שכינה was in בנימין's land and the סנהדרין in יהודה's.

keyTerms.meaning: What is his difficulty? (the challenge is not strong)
The Great סנהדרין, the high court of 71 judges
Since we have found (bringing a comparison)

steps.whatToRemember: רבי: the שכינה always rested in בנימין's land. רב יוסף objects that שילה is called 'the tent of יוסף'. רב אדא answers that the site was split: the שכינה in בנימין's land, the סנהדרין in יוסף's, just like the בית המקדש, which was split between בנימין and יהודה.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב אַדָּא: מַאי קָא קַשְׁיָא לֵיהּ?
phrases.english: Rav Adda said: What is his difficulty?
phrases.notes: 'His' means רב יוסף. רב אדא thinks the challenge doesn't really work.

phrases.english: Perhaps the Divine Presence was in the portion of Binyamin,
and the Great Sanhedrin in the portion of Yosef;
since we find in the Eternal House
that the Divine Presence was in the portion of Binyamin,
and the Sanhedrin in the portion of Yehuda!

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב אַדָּא: מַאי קָא קַשְׁיָא לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רב יוסף's challenge from step 11 and keeps רבי's teaching from step 10.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Split location: both פסוקים are true about different parts of the same site.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since the פסוק calls שילה 'the tent of יוסף', the שכינה must have been in יוסף's land.
steps.terutzMaskana: The שכינה was in בנימין's land, and the סנהדרין next to it was in יוסף's land, like the בית המקדש split between בנימין and יהודה.

steps.title: רב יוסף: the two cases are not alike
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף challenges רב אדא. In ירושלים the lands of יהודה and בנימין were right next to each other, but was שילה close to בנימין's land at all?
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: How can you compare? There, the tribal portions are close to each other. Here, are they close?
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף attacks the comparison רב אדא just made. He says the בית המקדש case only worked because two tribes' lands touched there.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב אדא said the שכינה and the סנהדרין can sit in two different tribes' lands, like at the בית המקדש. רב יוסף answers that this split only makes sense when the two lands touch. He doubts that שילה, in יוסף's land, was near enough to בנימין's land.

keyTerms.meaning: How can you compare? (rejects a comparison)

phrases.english: He said to him: How can you compare?!
phrases.notes: This is רב יוסף answering רב אדא from the last step.

phrases.english: There, the portions are close to each other;
phrases.notes: 'There' means the בית המקדש in ירושלים, where יהודה and בנימין met.

phrases.english: Here, are they close?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects רב אדא's comparison between שילה and the בית המקדש.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב אדא's comparison to the בית המקדש
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The split between the שכינה and the סנהדרין needs two lands that touch. That was true in ירושלים, but it seems untrue at שילה.

steps.title: They were close, like the strip under the מזבח
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the lands at שילה were close too. It first brings רבי חמא ברבי חנינא's teaching that a strip of יהודה's land reached into בנימין's land, and the מזבח was built on it.
steps.simpleTranslation: Here too they are close. As רבי חמא ברבי חנינא said: a strip went out from יהודה's portion into בנימין's portion, and the מזבח was built on it. בנימין the righteous was pained over it and wished to swallow it into his own land.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects רב יוסף's challenge and says the lands at שילה did touch. It first brings a model from the בית המקדש: a narrow strip of one tribe's land poking into another tribe's land.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The point of רבי חמא's teaching is that tribal borders were not simple straight lines. A strip could reach deep into a neighbor's land. That is why the מזבח stood on יהודה's strip inside בנימין's area. The next step will apply this same model to שילה.

keyTerms.meaning: to swallow it up (take it into his own land)

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two tribes here. The strip belonged to יהודה and stuck into בנימין's land. בנימין was upset because the holy spot was on יהודה's strip and not fully his.

phrases.english: Here too they are close.
As Rabbi Chama son of Rabbi Chanina said:

phrases.aramaic: רְצוּעָה הָיְתָה יוֹצֵאת מֵחֶלְקוֹ שֶׁל יְהוּדָה
phrases.english: A strip went out from the portion of Yehuda
and entered into the portion of Binyamin,
and on it the altar was built,

phrases.aramaic: וְהָיָה בִּנְיָמִין הַצַּדִּיק מִצְטַעֵר עָלֶיהָ לְבׇלְעָהּ.
phrases.english: and Binyamin the righteous was pained over it, wanting to swallow it up.
phrases.notes: He wanted that strip, with the holy מזבח on it, to be part of his own land.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָכָא נָמֵי מְקָרְבָן. כִּדְאָמַר רַבִּי חָמָא בְּרַבִּי חֲנִינָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רב יוסף's challenge by denying that שילה was far from בנימין's land.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Factual answer: the lands really did touch, with support from a known geographic teaching.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: שילה was deep in יוסף's land, far from בנימין's.
steps.terutzMaskana: Tribal lands could reach into each other through strips, as with the מזבח in ירושלים.

steps.title: A strip at שילה, hinted in 'תאנת שילה'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא applies the same model to שילה. A strip of יוסף's land went into בנימין's land, and the פסוק 'תאנת שילה' hints at this.
steps.simpleTranslation: Here too, a strip went out from יוסף's portion into בנימין's portion. That is what is written: 'תאנת שילה.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes its answer by saying the same kind of strip existed at שילה. It backs this up with a phrase from a פסוק in ספר יהושע.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Because of the strip, יוסף's land and בנימין's land met at שילה. So רב אדא's split works here too: the שכינה could be in בנימין's area while the סנהדרין was in יוסף's. The word תאנת is read as a hint to sorrow, the same kind of pain בנימין felt over the strip.

keyTerms.meaning: and that is what is written (a פסוק that fits)
a place name in the border of יוסף, read as a hint to sorrow

steps.whatToRemember: The lands of different tribes could meet through a strip of land. So the שכינה could rest in בנימין's land while the סנהדרין sat next door, both in ירושלים and at שילה.

phrases.english: Here too, a strip went out

phrases.aramaic: מֵחֶלְקוֹ שֶׁל יוֹסֵף, לְחֶלְקוֹ שֶׁל בִּנְיָמִין.
phrases.english: from the portion of Yosef into the portion of Binyamin.
And that is what is written: 'Taanath Shiloh.'
phrases.notes: יהושע 16:6. The word תאנת sounds like sorrow, hinting at בנימין's pain over not having all of שילה.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָכָא נָמֵי – רְצוּעָה הָיְתָה יוֹצֵאת מֵחֶלְקוֹ שֶׁל יוֹסֵף
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the ירושלים strip model from the last step to שילה.
steps.raayaObject: That a strip of יוסף's land reached into בנימין's land at שילה

steps.title: A dispute of תנאים: first view on 'חופף עליו'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא says this question is like a מחלוקת of תנאים. The first view reads the three parts of the פסוק as the first בית המקדש, the second בית המקדש, and the days of משיח.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is like a dispute of תנאים. 'He covers him' is the first מקדש. 'All the day' is the second מקדש. 'And He dwells between his shoulders' is the days of משיח.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows that the argument about שילה goes back to the תנאים. It brings the first of two readings of משה's ברכה to בנימין.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This תנא counts the שכינה resting in בנימין's land only from the first בית המקדש onward. He leaves out שילה, which fits רב יוסף's view that the משכן in שילה was in יוסף's land.

phrases.english: This is like a dispute of tanna'im:
'He covers him': this is the First Temple,
phrases.notes: דברים 33:12, משה's ברכה to בנימין.

phrases.english: 'All the day': this is the Second Temple,
'And He dwells between his shoulders': these are the days of the Messiah.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Steps back to show that the argument between רב דימי and רב יוסף matches an argument between תנאים.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: 'חופף עליו' begins with the first בית המקדש, so שילה is not counted as בנימין's land.

steps.title: רבי: the פסוק covers all of this world
steps.stepSummary: רבי reads the פסוק as this world, the days of משיח, and עולם הבא. On his reading, the שכינה always rested in בנימין's land, including at שילה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי says: 'He covers him' is this world. 'All the day' is the days of משיח. 'And He dwells between his shoulders' is עולם הבא.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings the second view, from רבי. His reading covers the whole time the שכינה rested in this world, so it includes שילה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Because 'this world' includes the time of שילה, רבי holds that the שכינה rested in בנימין's land then too. That matches exactly what רב דימי reported in רבי's name in Step 10. So רב דימי and רב יוסף are really arguing like these two תנאים.
steps.whatToRemember: The תנא קמא starts בנימין's privilege at the first בית המקדש, which leaves out שילה. רבי includes all of this world, שילה too. That is the source of רב דימי's teaching in רבי's name.

phrases.english: Rabbi says:
'He covers him': this is this world,
'All the day': these are the days of the Messiah,
'And He dwells between his shoulders': this is the World to Come.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the opposing reading of the same פסוק, which completes the מחלוקת תנאים.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: 'חופף עליו' means all of this world, so the שכינה rested in בנימין's land even at שילה.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The question of where the משכן in שילה stood is a מחלוקת תנאים. רב דימי follows רבי.

steps.title: A ברייתא counts the years of the אהל מועד in each place
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא gives the number of years the אהל מועד stood in each location: 39 in the מדבר, 14 in גלגל, and 57 in נוב and גבעון. That leaves 369 years for שילה.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן taught: The אהל מועד stood in the מדבר for forty years minus one. It stood in גלגל for fourteen years: seven years while they conquered the land and seven while they divided it. It stood in נוב and גבעון for fifty-seven years. So the years left over for שילה are three hundred seventy minus one.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that lists how many years the אהל מועד stood in each place. It then works out how many years are left for שילה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא builds on the פסוק that the בית המקדש was built in the 480th year after יציאת מצרים, which means 479 full years had passed. Subtracting 39, 14, and 57 from 479 leaves 370 minus one, which is 369, for שילה. The next steps will ask where each of these numbers comes from.

keyTerms.meaning: The Tent of Meeting, the משכן
The first camp after crossing the ירדן
The places where the משכן stood after שילה

steps.whyThisMatters: This timeline is the framework for the משנה's periods of היתר and איסור of private altars (במות). Each later step of the גמרא proves one of its numbers.

phrases.english: The Sages taught:
The days of the Tent of Meeting in the wilderness
were forty years, less one.

phrases.aramaic: יְמֵי אֹהֶל מוֹעֵד שֶׁבַּגִּלְגָּל – אַרְבַּע עֶשְׂרֵה;
phrases.english: The days of the Tent of Meeting in Gilgal were fourteen;
seven that they conquered, and seven that they divided.

phrases.aramaic: יְמֵי אֹהֶל מוֹעֵד שֶׁבְּנוֹב וְגִבְעוֹן – חֲמִשִּׁים וָשֶׁבַע.
phrases.english: The days of the Tent of Meeting in Nov and Gibeon were fifty-seven.
There remain for Shiloh
phrases.notes: Left over from the years between יציאת מצרים and the בית המקדש, which was built in the 480th year (מלכים א 6:1).

phrases.english: three hundred and seventy, less one.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: יְמֵי אֹהֶל מוֹעֵד שֶׁבַּמִּדְבָּר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new section that sets out the timeline of the משכן's locations.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: מדבר 39 years, גלגל 14, נוב and גבעון 57, so שילה gets the remaining 369 years before the בית המקדש was built in the 480th year.

steps.title: Where do we know the 39 years in the מדבר from?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the source that the אהל מועד stood in the מדבר for 39 years.
steps.simpleTranslation: The ברייתא said the אהל מועד stood in the מדבר for forty years minus one. How do we know this?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the first number in the ברייתא and asks for its source. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Everyone knows the Jews were in the מדבר for forty years. The question is why the ברייתא subtracts one year.

keyTerms.meaning: From where do we know this?

phrases.english: The days of the Tent of Meeting in the wilderness
were forty, less one.
From where do we know this?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the source of the first number in the ברייתא.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The source that the משכן in the מדבר stood for 39 years, not 40.

steps.title: The משכן went up only in the second year
steps.stepSummary: A teaching says משה built the משכן in the first year and set it up in the second year, so it stood for only 39 of the 40 years.
steps.simpleTranslation: As the Master said: In the first year משה made the משכן. In the second year the משכן was set up, and משה sent the spies.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers with a teaching that the משכן was only set up in the second year after יציאת מצרים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The Jews were in the מדבר for 40 years, but the first year was spent building the משכן. So it actually stood for only 39 years. The detail that the spies were sent in that same second year will be used for the next calculation.

phrases.english: As the Master said:

phrases.aramaic: שָׁנָה רִאשׁוֹנָה – עָשָׂה מֹשֶׁה אֶת הַמִּשְׁכָּן,
phrases.english: In the first year, Moses made the Tabernacle;
in the second, the Tabernacle was set up,
and Moses sent spies.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 19.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The משכן was set up only in year two, so it stood for 39 of the 40 years.

steps.title: Where do we know the 14 years in גלגל from?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the source that the משכן stood in גלגל for 14 years: seven of conquest and seven of dividing the land.
steps.simpleTranslation: The ברייתא said the משכן stood in גלגל for fourteen years, seven of conquering and seven of dividing. How do we know this?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to the second number in the ברייתא and asks for its source. The answer follows in the next steps.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Two separate facts need a source here: seven years of conquest and seven years of dividing the land.

phrases.english: That in Gilgal it was fourteen,
seven that they conquered and seven that they divided.
From where do we know this?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After proving the מדבר number, the גמרא turns to the גלגל number.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The source for seven years of conquest and seven years of dividing.

steps.title: כלב's two ages in ספר יהושע
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes כלב: he was 40 when משה sent him as a spy, and he was 85 when the land was being divided.
steps.simpleTranslation: כלב said: 'I was forty years old when משה, the servant of ה׳, sent me from קדש ברנע to spy out the land, and I brought back word as it was in my heart.' And it is written: 'And now, here I am today, eighty-five years old.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings two פסוקים where כלב states his age at two different times. These are the raw data for the calculation in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first פסוק fixes כלב's age, 40, in the year of the spies. That was the second year, as the previous step taught. The second פסוק gives his age, 85, when the conquest was finished, so the difference can be used to count years.

keyTerms.meaning: כלב בן יפונה, one of the two faithful spies
The place in the מדבר the spies were sent from

phrases.english: As Caleb said:
"Forty years old was I
when Moses, the servant of the Lord, sent me
from Kadesh Barnea to spy out the land,

phrases.aramaic: וָאָשֵׁב אוֹתוֹ דָּבָר כַּאֲשֶׁר עִם לְבָבִי״;
phrases.english: and I brought him back word as it was in my heart";
phrases.notes: יהושע 14:7

phrases.aramaic: וּכְתִיב: ״וְעַתָּה הִנֵּה אָנֹכִי הַיּוֹם בֶּן חָמֵשׁ וּשְׁמֹנִים שָׁנָה״.
phrases.english: and it is written: "And now, behold, I am today eighty-five years old."
phrases.notes: יהושע 14:10

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins answering step 21 with פסוקים.
steps.raayaObject: The seven years of conquest in גלגל
steps.raayaSupportSource: יהושע 14:7 and 14:10, where כלב gives his age

steps.title: The math proves seven years of conquest
steps.stepSummary: כלב was 78 when they crossed the ירדן and 85 at the end of the conquest, so the conquest took seven years.
steps.simpleTranslation: When they crossed the ירדן, how old was כלב? Seventy-eight. And he says he is eighty-five. So that makes seven years of conquering.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא does the math with כלב's ages. It shows that the conquest of the land took seven years.
steps.deeperAnalysis: כלב was 40 in the second year. The crossing of the ירדן came in the fortieth year, 38 years later, so he was then 78. Going from 78 to 85 gives seven years. This proves only the first seven years in גלגל; the seven years of dividing still need a source.
steps.whatToRemember: כלב was 40 at the spies and 78 at the ירדן crossing. He was 85 after the conquest, so the conquest took seven years.
steps.confusionAlert: This step proves only the seven years of conquest, not the seven years of dividing the land.

phrases.english: When they crossed the Jordan,
how old was he?
Seventy-eight years old,
and he says: "eighty-five years old";
so there are seven that they conquered.

steps.triggerLanguage: כִּי עַבְרֵיהּ לְיַרְדֵּן בַּר כַּמָּה הָוֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the ages from step 22 and the year of the spies from step 20 to work out the length of the conquest.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The conquest of the land took seven years, which is the first half of the 14 years in גלגל.

steps.title: Where do we know the land was divided over seven years?
steps.stepSummary: After proving seven years of conquest, the גמרא asks for a source for the other seven years, the years of dividing the land.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the seven years in which they divided the land, where do we learn that from?
steps.whatsHappening: כלב's ages proved only the seven years of conquest. Now the גמרא asks how we know the dividing also took seven years, which is needed to reach 14 years in גלגל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The claim was 14 years in גלגל: 7 conquering plus 7 dividing. The ages of כלב only covered the first seven. This question sets up the next step, which gives two possible answers.

keyTerms.meaning: that they divided (the land among the שבטים)
from where do we know this?

phrases.english: And the seven years that they divided the land, from where do we know it?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Step 23 proved the first half of the 14 years (conquest). This step asks for the second half (dividing).
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A source that dividing the land took seven years.

steps.title: First answer: dividing matched the seven years of conquering
steps.stepSummary: Since conquering took seven years, dividing the land also took seven years.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you want, say: since they conquered for seven years, they also divided for seven years.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a first answer. The dividing took the same amount of time as the conquering.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This answer is a logical match, not a פסוק. The land was conquered bit by bit over seven years, so dividing it fairly would take about the same time.

keyTerms.meaning: if you want, say this (gives one of two possible answers)

phrases.english: If you want, say: since there were seven years that they conquered,
there were also seven years that they divided.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question in step 24 using the result of step 23.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Dividing took the same seven years as conquering.

steps.title: Second answer: the date in יחזקאל's prophecy
steps.stepSummary: Another proof: otherwise the date יחזקאל gives, 'in the fourteenth year after the city was struck', does not make sense.
steps.simpleTranslation: Or if you want, say: we know it because otherwise you cannot explain the 'fourteenth year after the city was struck' in יחזקאל.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a second, different answer. It is based on a date written in a פסוק in יחזקאל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: יחזקאל's vision is dated in a way that points to a יובל year. That only works if the count of שמיטה and יובל started 14 years after the people entered the land. So conquering plus dividing must have taken 14 years, which leaves seven years for the dividing.

keyTerms.meaning: you can find it (here: you can make sense of it)
the city was struck (ירושלים was destroyed)

steps.confusionAlert: The 'fourteen years' in יחזקאל are counted from the destruction of ירושלים, not from the days of יהושע. The proof works only through the יובל calendar, which began after 14 years in the land.

phrases.english: And if you want, say: because otherwise you cannot find a way to explain

phrases.aramaic: בְּאַרְבַּע עֶשְׂרֵה שָׁנָה ״אַחַר אֲשֶׁר הֻכְּתָה הָעִיר״.
phrases.english: 'in the fourteenth year after the city was struck.'
phrases.notes: יחזקאל 40:1

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second, separate answer to the question in step 24, given instead of the logical answer in step 25.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The יובל date in יחזקאל only works if conquering and dividing together took 14 years.
steps.whatToRemember: The 14 years in גלגל are 7 years of conquest (proved from כלב's ages) plus 7 years of dividing (proved from logic or from the date in יחזקאל).

steps.title: Where do we know the משכן stood 57 years in נוב and גבעון?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא moves to the next number in the ברייתא and asks for the source of the 57 years in נוב and גבעון.
steps.simpleTranslation: The אהל מועד in נוב and גבעון stood 57 years. How do we know this?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new section. It quotes the next part of the ברייתא and asks for its source.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This follows the same pattern as before: the ברייתא gave a number for each place, and the גמרא proves each one in order. Here the number covers both נוב and גבעון together.

keyTerms.meaning: the city where the משכן stood after שילה
the city where the משכן stood after נוב

phrases.english: The Tent of Meeting that was in נוב and גבעון:
fifty-seven years. From where do we know this?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֹהֶל מוֹעֵד שֶׁבְּנוֹב וְגִבְעוֹן חֲמִשִּׁים וָשֶׁבַע מְנָא לַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After finishing the 14 years of גלגל, the גמרא moves on to the next period in the ברייתא.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A source for the 57 years of the משכן in נוב and גבעון.

steps.title: The פסוק about the death of עלי
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the פסוק describing עלי's death when he heard the ארון was captured. This marks the start of the נוב period.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it is written: 'And when he mentioned the ארון of God...' (and עלי fell and died).
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins its proof with a פסוק that marks a starting point in time: the day עלי died.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ארון was captured and עלי died that day. This is the event that ended the שילה period, so it is where the count of the 57 years begins.

phrases.english: As it is written: 'And it was, when he mentioned the ארון of God.'
phrases.notes: שמואל א 4:18. When the messenger mentioned the captured ארון, עלי fell and died.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts answering step 27 by fixing the starting point of the period.
steps.raayaObject: The start of the 57 years in נוב and גבעון.
steps.raayaSupportSource: שמואל א 4:18, the death of עלי.

steps.title: Each move of the משכן followed a leader's death
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches: when עלי died, שילה was destroyed and they came to נוב; when שמואל died, נוב was destroyed and they came to גבעון.
steps.simpleTranslation: And a תנא taught: When עלי the כהן died, שילה was destroyed and they came to נוב. When שמואל from רמה died, נוב was destroyed and they came to גבעון.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds a teaching that ties each move of the משכן to someone's death. This gives fixed points in time for counting the years.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now we know the נוב period ran from עלי's death to שמואל's death. After that the גבעון period began. The גמרא is setting up the counting of years between these events to reach 57.

keyTerms.meaning: the city where the משכן stood before נוב

phrases.english: And a תנא taught: When עלי the כהן died,
שילה was destroyed, and they came to נוב.
When שמואל from רמה died,
נוב was destroyed, and they came to גבעון.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on the פסוק about עלי's death by adding the timeline of each move of the משכן.
steps.raayaObject: The time markers for the נוב and גבעון periods.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא linking the destruction of שילה to עלי's death and the destruction of נוב to שמואל's death.
steps.whyThisMatters: These two deaths are the anchors the גמרא will use to count out the 57 years.

steps.title: The ארון stayed in קרית יערים for twenty years
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes a פסוק saying the ארון was in קרית יערים for twenty years. This gives a fixed length of time to build the count on.
steps.simpleTranslation: And it is written: 'From the day the ארון stayed in קרית יערים, a long time passed, twenty years, and all of בית ישראל yearned after ה׳.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second פסוק to help count the years. It is setting up the next step, where those twenty years get split up.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The earlier steps showed that the נוב period starts when עלי died, around the time the ארון was captured. This פסוק adds a fixed number: the ארון stayed in קרית יערים for twenty years. The גמרא will now use that number as a measuring stick for the years of נוב and גבעון.

steps.title: Splitting up the twenty years
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא divides the twenty years: ten for שמואל alone, one for שמואל and שאול together, two for שאול alone, and seven for דוד.
steps.simpleTranslation: These twenty years are: ten years that שמואל ruled by himself, one year that שמואל and שאול ruled together, two years that שאול ruled alone, and the seven years of דוד.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains which years make up the twenty years from the פסוק. The thought is not finished yet; it continues on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The twenty years are cut into pieces that line up with the leaders of that time: 10 + 1 + 2 + 7 = 20. These pieces link the ארון's time in קרית יערים to the reigns of שמואל, שאול and דוד. That lets the גמרא tie the time of נוב and גבעון to known lengths of rule.
steps.confusionAlert: שמואל and שאול overlap for one year. Do not count that year twice. The list gives שמואל alone, then the two of them together, then שאול alone.
